articles.title_zh: Brazil election goes to run-off as right-wing Flávio Bolsonaro wins first round
facts_zh:
Brazil election goes to run-off as right-wing Flávio Bolsonaro wins first round
- Published
The right-wing Flávio Bolsonaro has won the first round of Brazil's presidential election, beating the incumbent left-wing President Lula da Silva.
But he did not obtain more than 50% of the votes required to win outright.
There will be a run-off vote between these two candidates on 25 October.

articles.title_original: Brazil’s presidential race goes to second round as Flávio Bolsonaro leads incumbent Lula
articles.title_zh: Brazil’s presidential race goes to second round as Flávio Bolsonaro leads incumbent Lula
facts_zh: Far-right challenger and son of disgraced ex-president Jair Bolsonaro will now face leftwing president in runoff vote Brazil’s presidential race will go to a second round after the far-right candidate, Flávio Bolsonaro, beat the incumbent leftwing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, but failed to secure the outright majority he needed to avoid a runoff.
With more than 99% of votes counted, the 45-year-old son of the disgraced former president, Jair Bolsonaro, had won 47.1%, meaning he will now face a 25 October showdown with his 80-year-old rival.
Lula received 45%.

articles.title_zh: Rescuers suspend search for survivors after plane went missing off US coast
facts_zh:
Rescuers suspend search for survivors after plane went missing off US coast
- Published
US authorities have suspended the search for six people aboard a medical transport aircraft that went missing on Saturday while it was travelling from Bermuda to Boston.
The Coast Guard said on Sunday evening it was ending the search off the coast of Nantucket, a Massachusetts island, after 66 hours of looking for the passengers.
"We express our deepest condolences to the families and loved ones," the Coast Guard said on Sunday.

What to know about Brazil's election as Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro face off
- Published
Brazilians just finished voting in a general election in which the two front-runners for the presidency bear very familiar names.
Polls closed at 17:00 Brasília Time (20:00 GMT) on Sunday, with the nation's vast electronic voter system expected to deliver a result within a few hours.
The incumbent, veteran left-wing leader Luíz Inácio Lula da Silva, is challenged by 11 candidates, the most prominent of whom is right-winger Flávio Bolsonaro.

articles.title_zh: Indian police accused of sexually harassing journalists at protest
facts_zh:
Indian police accused of sexually harassing journalists at protest
- Published
Three female journalists have accused police officers in India of sexual harassment during street protests in the capital Delhi.
The claims were made on Saturday after the force detained scores of young people calling for the resignation of the chief election commissioner.
In a post on social media, Delhi Police said its New Delhi District had received the complaint, and it had been transferred to its crime branch for a "fair and impartial" inquiry.

all_titles.en: Indian police accused of sexually harassing journalists at protest

articles.title_zh: Yemen's government announces all-out war to reclaim land from Houthis
facts_zh:
Yemen's government announces all-out war to reclaim land from Houthis
- Published
The head of Yemen's internationally recognised government has announced it will wage an all out war in an effort to take all territory held by the Houthis.
It follows an exchange of strikes between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition in recent days.
The Iran-backed group said it had struck sites belonging to Saudi national oil company Aramco, in response to what it described as 50 Saudi-led coalition strikes in 12 hours.

articles.title_zh: Christa Pike's prognosis still unclear after failed execution, lawyer says
facts_zh:
Christa Pike's prognosis still unclear after failed execution, lawyer says
- Published
US murderer Christa Pike remains critically ill in hospital and her prognosis is still unclear following her failed execution, her lawyer has said on Sunday.
Speaking to CNN on Sunday morning, Pike's lawyer Stephen Ferrell said doctors were still trying to clear two doses of pentobarbital from her body.
Pike, 50, was sentenced to death following her conviction for murdering Colleen Slemmer in 1995.

articles.title_zh: US Marine arrested over murder of woman in Okinawa, Japan
facts_zh:
US Marine arrested over murder of woman in Okinawa, Japan
- Published
A US Marine has been arrested on suspicion of murder after a woman's body was found in a hotel in Okinawa, Japan, local officials say.
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi described the crime as a "brutal and heinous" robbery and murder.
She said she had urged the US to "enforce stricter discipline" of its personnel.

articles.title_original: Watch: What we know about Russian strikes on Kyiv bridges
articles.title_zh: Watch: What we know about Russian strikes on Kyiv bridges
facts_zh:
Watch: What we know about Russian strikes on Kyiv bridges
Major bridges in Ukraine have been the target of Russian strikes over the past four days, as Moscow ramps up attacks in Ukraine's capital city.
The Pivnichnyi (Northern) Bridge, has been hit for the second day in a row, while the Pivdennyi (Southern) Bridge was hit multiple times earlier this week.
The latest attack came as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz made a visit to Kyiv on Sunday.
